html:
Wallachia was a Romanian principality between the Southern Carpathians and the lower Danube, from the 1300s to 1859. It is on the map for 1400.

Its founder, Basarab I, won independence from Hungary by beating a Hungarian army at Posada in 1330. Around 1400 its prince was Mircea the Elder, who ruled from 1386 to 1418. He fought the Ottomans at Rovine in 1395, joined the crusade that failed at Nicopolis in 1396, and in the end agreed to pay the sultan tribute.

From then on Wallachia was mostly an Ottoman vassal with its own princes, who often fought for the throne. The most famous was Vlad the Impaler in the 1400s. In 1859 Wallachia joined Moldavia to form Romania.
sum: Wallachia was a Romanian principality between the Southern Carpathians and the lower Danube, from the 1300s to 1859. It is on the map for 1400.
